correctness.rationale: The proof defines the unit-edge graph and Lipschitz potentials, derives integrality of extreme potential values from a connected tight spanning graph, splits into constant-clique (six) and two-level clique (eight for each nonempty proper subset) cases, and establishes all cases are tight-connected. It counts signed symmetry orbits with explicit sizes and maximizes the exact tight-edge count. The exact stand-alone code enumerates all potential classes via a finite distance bound and confirms all claimed statistics at n=5 through 10. Finite tests are not used as proof for all n.

value.rationale: One-edge subdivision of a complete graph is a canonical local metric operation on a highly symmetric finite Banach-space model. The simultaneous exact facet count, full signed graph-symmetry orbit-size list and sharp vertex incidence extremum solve natural structural invariants across every order n≥5. Linear orbit growth against exponential total growth reveals information not inherent in the generic facet criterion and is not an arbitrary finite slice or numeric micro-gain.
